questions.subtopic: Workflow Start — Cube Root Workflow Profile
questions.question: What must be configured on a cube before an administrator can create a Cube Root Workflow Profile?

options.A: A business rule must be assigned to the cube
options.B: A corresponding cube type must be defined
options.C: Is Top Level Cube For Workflow must be set to True
options.D: The cube must have at least two Scenario Types assigned

questions.explanation: C is correct: the 'Is Top Level Cube For Workflow' property on the cube must be set to True before a Cube Root Workflow Profile can be created for that cube — this setting designates the cube as eligible to serve as the top-level root for workflow hierarchies. A is incorrect — a business rule is not required before creating a Cube Root Workflow Profile; business rules are assigned to workflow steps as needed. B is incorrect — defining a cube type is not a prerequisite; the Is Top Level Cube setting is the specific required configuration. D is incorrect — multiple Scenario Types are not required; a single cube with the Is Top Level Cube flag set to True is sufficient.

questions.question: What is automatically created when a Cube Root Workflow Profile is created, and should always be preserved?
questions.explanation: C is correct: when a Cube Root Workflow Profile is created, OneStream automatically generates a corresponding Default Workflow Profile (for example: Corporate_Default) — this profile establishes the relationship between the workflow hierarchy and the entity members in the cube, is required for each workflow hierarchy, and cannot be deleted. A is incorrect — no Cube View profile is automatically generated from a Cube Root Workflow Profile. B is incorrect — no new cube is created; the Cube Root profile is built on an existing cube. D is incorrect — transformation rules are configured separately in the data integration setup, not auto-generated from workflow profiles.

questions.question: What is the Default Workflow Profile used for in OneStream?

options.A: To be configured for loading and inputting data
options.C: To act as a child and/or sibling template when building out the workflow
options.D: To define which entities are assigned to the workflow

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Default Workflow Profile is used by OneStream to calculate workflow status — it should not be modified because changes may lead to complications with out-of-the-box functionality and OneStream Support. A is incorrect — the Default Workflow Profile is not configured for data loading or input; those functions are handled by Base Input and Import child workflow profiles. C is incorrect — the Default Workflow Profile is not used as a template for building child or sibling workflows; Workflow Templates serve that purpose. D is incorrect — entity assignments are handled on the individual Base Input Workflow Profiles, not on the Default profile.

questions.question: Where can an administrator configure Workflow Templates within the OneStream application?

options.B: Application > Workflow > Workflow Profiles > Work With Templates

questions.explanation: B is correct: Workflow Templates are configured through Application > Workflow > Workflow Profiles > Work With Templates — they are useful when building a series of Base Input Workflow Profiles with similar settings, and can be generic or customized before being applied to new workflows. A is incorrect — Application Properties contains general application settings such as currency and number format, not Workflow Templates. C is incorrect — the Default Workflow Profile is system-managed and should not be modified; templates are configured through Work With Templates, not within the Default profile. D is incorrect — the System tab is for system-level administration, not workflow template configuration.

questions.question: An administrator has added a new input type to an existing workflow template. How is the new input type applied to existing Workflow Profiles?

options.B: Choose Create a Sibling of the Current Workflow
options.C: Choose Update Input Children Using Template
options.D: Delete and recreate the affected Workflow Profiles

questions.explanation: C is correct: the 'Update Input Children Using Template' option allows the administrator to select a template with the new input types and specify which Workflow Profiles should receive the changes — pushing the template update out to existing profiles. A is incorrect — Work With Profiles is used for general profile management, not for applying template updates to existing profiles. B is incorrect — Create a Sibling creates a new parallel workflow profile; it does not update existing ones with template changes. D is incorrect — deleting and recreating profiles would lose all existing configuration; the Update Input Children Using Template option handles this non-destructively.

questions.question: What are the three main Workflow Profile Types in OneStream?

options.B: Base Input, Parent Input, and Review
options.D: Cube Root, Default, and Base Input

questions.explanation: B is correct: the three main Workflow Profile Types are Base Input, Parent Input, and Review — each serves a distinct role in the data collection and review hierarchy. A is incorrect — Import, Forms, and Adj are the Input Child Workflow Profile Types that exist within a Base Input Workflow Profile, not the main profile types themselves. C is incorrect — BeforeElim, DirectElim, and IndirectElim are Consolidation Types related to intercompany elimination, not Workflow Profile Types. D is incorrect — Cube Root and Default are structural profiles that establish the workflow hierarchy framework, not the three main types used for data collection and review.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Start — Input Child Profile Types
questions.question: Which Input Child Workflow Profile Types are included within a Base Input Workflow Profile?

options.A: Base Input, Parent Input, and Review

questions.explanation: B is correct: Import, Forms, and Adj are the three Input Child Workflow Profile Types contained within a Base Input Workflow Profile — Import handles file-based data loading, Forms handles manual data entry, and Adj handles adjusting entries. A is incorrect — Base Input, Parent Input, and Review are the main Workflow Profile Types, not the child types within a Base Input profile. C is incorrect — BeforeElim, DirectElim, and IndirectElim are Consolidation Types, not workflow child types. D is incorrect — Validate, Process, and Confirm are workflow steps (tasks within a profile), not profile types.

questions.question: Which Workflow Profile Type lacks a direct relationship to an Entity member or Origin member?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Review Workflow Profile Type does not have a direct relationship to Entity or Origin members — common uses include reviewing, confirming, and certifying results from lower-level input workflow profiles rather than collecting data for specific entities. A is incorrect — Base Input Workflow Profiles have a direct relationship to entity members through Entity Assignments; they collect data for specific entities. B is incorrect — Parent Input Workflow Profiles are associated with parent entity members for top-side adjustments. D is incorrect — Import is a child type within Base Input and is tied to the entity dimension through the parent Base Input profile.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Start — Base Input Profile Tabs
questions.question: What tabs become accessible at the parent level when a Base Input Workflow Profile is selected within the workflow hierarchy?

options.A: Profile Properties, Entity Assignment, and Grid View
options.B: Profile Properties and Calculation Definitions only
options.C: Profile Properties, Calculation Definitions, and Entity Assignments

questions.explanation: C is correct: Profile Properties, Calculation Definitions, and Entity Assignments are the three tabs available at the parent level of a Base Input Workflow Profile — together they allow the administrator to configure the profile's behavior, calculations, and entity scope. A is incorrect — Grid View is a view available at the Cube Root level for bulk edits, not a tab at the Base Input parent level. B is incorrect — while Profile Properties and Calculation Definitions are both present, Entity Assignments is also available and is essential for linking the profile to specific entities. D is incorrect — Integration and Security are not the standard tabs shown at the parent level of a Base Input profile.

questions.question: What is the Workflow Name property used for in a Workflow Profile?

options.A: To allow a user to apply a unique description to a Workflow Profile
options.B: To control the tasks that users need to complete in their workflows
options.C: To apply a unique name to a Workflow Profile for display purposes only
options.D: To link the Workflow Profile to a specific cube

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Workflow Name property plays a central role in a Workflow Profile because it defines the specific set of tasks a user must complete — it controls which workflow steps appear and are required for that profile. A is incorrect — the description field is separate from the Workflow Name; descriptions are optional metadata and do not control task behavior. C is incorrect — the Workflow Name is not merely a display label; it actively determines which tasks are required in the workflow. D is incorrect — linking to a cube is done through the Cube Root Workflow Profile structure and cube assignments, not through the Workflow Name property.

questions.question: What property must be set to True to enable a Central Input Import Workflow Profile to import data for entities not assigned to its parent Workflow Profile?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the 'Can Load Unrelated Entities' property must be set to True — when enabled, a Central Input Import Workflow Profile can load data to entities that are not assigned to its parent Input Workflow Profile, supporting centralized data loading for multiple entities from one workflow. A is incorrect — 'Is Optional Data Load' controls whether the import step is optional in the workflow, not whether it can load data for unrelated entities. B is incorrect — Profile Active determines whether the workflow profile is enabled or disabled, not its entity loading scope. C is incorrect — Matching Enabled is related to intercompany matching configuration, not entity loading scope for Central Input workflows.

questions.question: Which steps must be taken to disable Adj in a workflow template?

options.A: Select the Adj input in the workflow, then remove the name in the Workflow Name property
options.B: Select the Adj input in the workflow, then set the Profile Active property to False in the Workflow Profile Settings
options.C: Right-click the Adj input in the workflow and select Disable
options.D: Delete the Adj input from the workflow template entirely

questions.explanation: B is correct: to disable Adj in a workflow template, the administrator first selects the Adj input in the workflow and then sets the Profile Active property to False in the Workflow Profile Settings — this deactivates the input without deleting it, preserving the configuration if it needs to be re-enabled. A is incorrect — removing the Workflow Name property value would break the workflow's task definition; Profile Active is the correct toggle for enabling/disabling an input. C is incorrect — there is no right-click 'Disable' option for workflow profile inputs; the Profile Active setting is the correct mechanism. D is incorrect — deleting the Adj input entirely removes the configuration permanently; setting Profile Active to False is the preferred non-destructive approach.

questions.question: What does a workflow hierarchy coordinate in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a workflow hierarchy coordinates end-user activities in OneStream — it organizes and sequences the tasks that users perform during the data collection, review, and certification process. A is incorrect — dashboard creation is handled through the Workspaces and Dashboard Maintenance Units, not the workflow hierarchy. C is incorrect — user roles are managed through security groups and role assignments, not the workflow hierarchy. D is incorrect — report generation is handled through Cube Views, Report Books, and dashboards, not coordinated by the workflow hierarchy.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Start — Building a Workflow Hierarchy
questions.question: What is the first step in defining a workflow hierarchy in OneStream?

options.A: Creating a Cube Root Workflow Profile

questions.explanation: A is correct: creating a Cube Root Workflow Profile is the first step in defining a workflow hierarchy — the Cube Root profile establishes the top-level structure, and from it the Default Workflow Profile is automatically generated, forming the foundation for all subsequent child and sibling profiles. B is incorrect — sibling profiles are added after the hierarchy foundation is established, not as the first step. C is incorrect — the Default Workflow Profile is automatically created when the Cube Root is created; it is not manually created as the first step. D is incorrect — child profiles are built after the Cube Root and Default profiles are in place.

questions.question: What does the Workflow Name property determine in a OneStream Workflow Profile?

options.A: The reports generated by the workflow
options.C: The dashboards created by the workflow
options.D: The users assigned to the workflow

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Workflow Name property determines the tasks required in the workflow — it defines which specific set of steps (Validate, Process, Confirm, Certify, etc.) the user must complete for that profile. A is incorrect — report generation is controlled by Cube Views, Report Books, and dashboards, not by the Workflow Name. C is incorrect — dashboards are configured in Workspaces and assigned through dashboard profiles, not through the Workflow Name. D is incorrect — user assignments to workflows are handled through security groups and entity assignments in the workflow profile, not the Workflow Name property.

questions.question: When is a Central Input workflow used in OneStream?

options.A: When large companies with multiple entities have a central corporate office loading or inputting data for several entities through one central workflow
options.B: When smaller companies with multiple entities have several offices loading data for multiple entities through one central workflow
options.C: It is recommended to always use a Central Input workflow regardless of company size
options.D: When a company wants to prevent individual entities from entering their own data

questions.explanation: A is correct: a Central Input workflow is specifically designed for large companies with multiple entities where a central corporate office handles loading or inputting data for several entities through a single centralized workflow — the Can Load Unrelated Entities property enables this cross-entity capability. B is incorrect — Central Input is designed for large companies with centralized data management, not smaller companies with distributed offices. C is incorrect — Central Input is not universally recommended; it is appropriate only for specific organizational structures. D is incorrect — prevention of entity-level data entry is a security function, not the purpose of Central Input workflows.

questions.subtopic: Workflow Start — Workflow Templates for Efficiency
questions.question: An administrator has an ongoing need to build Workflow Profiles with a similar structure. What should they use to speed up development time when building new workflows?

options.B: Workflow Profiles copied from the Default

questions.explanation: C is correct: Workflow Templates are the tool designed to speed up development when building multiple Workflow Profiles with similar structures — a template can be configured once with the common settings and then applied to new Base Input Workflow Profiles. A is incorrect — 'Template Base Inputs' is not a named OneStream feature; the correct term is Workflow Templates. B is incorrect — copying from the Default Workflow Profile is not the recommended approach and risks altering a system-managed profile. D is incorrect — Data Management Sequences orchestrate data processing steps, not workflow profile creation.

questions.question: An administrator needs to enable a dimension for a cube to allow data to be imported to that dimension. Which property of the cube Integration tab should be set to True?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the 'Enabled' property on the cube Integration tab must be set to True to allow data to be imported for that dimension — this is where default data integration properties are configured for the application and for properties that differ by Scenario Type. A is incorrect — Profile Active is a Workflow Profile property that controls whether a profile is active or disabled; it is not on the cube Integration tab. B is incorrect — 'Activate' is not the correct property name; 'Enabled' is the correct setting. D is incorrect — Is Optional Data Load is a Workflow Profile property, not a cube Integration tab setting.

questions.subtopic: Importing Data — Cube Integration Tab Sections
questions.question: Which sections in the cube Integration tab are used to load additional detail to the stage that will be excluded from storage in the cube?

options.B: Label Dimensions, Attribute Dimensions, and Attribute Value Dimensions
options.C: Cube Dimensions, Attribute Dimensions, and Attribute Value Dimensions
options.D: Label Dimensions and Attribute Dimensions only

questions.explanation: B is correct: Label Dimensions, Attribute Dimensions, and Attribute Value Dimensions are the three sections used to load additional detail to the stage that will be excluded from storage in the cube — this detail enriches the staging area for reporting without increasing cube storage. A is incorrect — Cube Dimensions are the standard dimensions that define cube data storage; they are not the sections for stage-only additional detail. C is incorrect — including Cube Dimensions in this list is incorrect; they are for cube storage, not stage-only enrichment. D is incorrect — Attribute Value Dimensions must also be included; Label and Attribute alone are not the complete set.

questions.question: Which type of transformation rule would an administrator use to map a delimited list of source entities to a single target entity?
questions.explanation: D is correct: List mapping allows the administrator to create a delimited list of source members that all map to the same target — this is the appropriate rule when multiple source values should consolidate to one target. A is incorrect — Composite rules combine multiple dimension values into a single mapping key, which is different from a list-to-one mapping. B is incorrect — Mask rules use wildcard characters to match patterns across source values, not a specific delimited list. C is incorrect — One-To-One mapping explicitly maps a single source member to a single target member; it does not handle multiple source values.

questions.question: What is the purpose of transformation rules in OneStream?

options.A: To tell OneStream where to read the data from
options.B: To transform Cube View Profiles into transformation rule profiles
options.C: To map data from source systems to the financial model
options.D: To transform the source data into a machine-readable format

questions.explanation: C is correct: transformation rules map data from source systems to the financial model — they translate source member names and values into the corresponding OneStream dimension members and intersections used for reporting and analysis. A is incorrect — where to read data from is determined by the Data Source configuration, not transformation rules. B is incorrect — there is no concept of transforming Cube View Profiles into transformation rule profiles; these are distinct objects. D is incorrect — data format conversion is a data source function; transformation rules operate on mapped values, not the raw format.

questions.subtopic: Importing Data — Import Workflow Profile Assignments
questions.question: Which two items are assigned to the Import Workflow Profile? (Select 2.)
questions.explanation: B and D are correct: a Data source and a Transformation profile are the two items assigned to the Import Workflow Profile — the Data source specifies where the data comes from, and the Transformation profile contains the transformation group(s) that define how the data maps to the financial model. A is incorrect — transformation groups are contained within transformation profiles; the profile is what is assigned, not individual groups directly. C is incorrect — individual transformation rules are organized into groups within a transformation profile; the profile is what is assigned, not individual rules.

questions.question: Where would an administrator navigate to edit Workflow Profile properties in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Workflow Profile properties are edited by navigating to Application > Workflow > Workflow Profiles — this is the administrative path for managing all workflow configuration. A is incorrect — OnePlace is the end-user-facing navigation area for completing workflow tasks, not for editing profile properties. B is incorrect — 'Application > Data Collection' is not the correct menu path; the path is Application > Workflow. D is incorrect — the System tab contains system-level settings, not workflow profile administration.

questions.question: Which data load method only adds rows that were excluded in the previous file load, without changing any data already loaded for the source file?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Append will not change any data already loaded for the source file — it only adds rows that were not included in the previous load, making it ideal for incremental data additions without disturbing existing data. A is incorrect — Replace (All Time) clears and replaces all data for the source across all time periods; it does not preserve existing data. B is incorrect — Replace clears and reloads data for the current time period; it overwrites existing data rather than adding to it. D is incorrect — Merge is not a standard OneStream data load method designation in this context.

questions.question: Using the Process Log codes, what is the cause of an error that displays Log Code 7?

options.A: A blank value in the source data
options.B: A non-numeric amount in the source data

questions.explanation: C is correct: Log Code 7 indicates an Invalid DataKey (Scenario) error — the Scenario value in the source data does not match a valid Scenario in the OneStream application. A is incorrect — a blank value corresponds to Log Code 1 (Blank) per the Process Log code table. B is incorrect — a non-numeric amount corresponds to Log Code 4 (Non-Numeric Amount). D is incorrect — Time outside the Workflow View corresponds to Log Code 11; Scenario outside the Workflow View is Log Code 10.
